title: WOMEN'S BASKETBALL | Sam Purcell, Madison Francis vs Buffalo - 11/14/26
text: Uh Diane Jackson is another good one. How was it preparing for him and how do you think y'all executed? >> Yeah, I mean um preparation was the same preparation that we have for every game. Um we have an amazing scout um with our staff. Um they do an amazing job um scouting each team. Um and I feel like we exe executed well. Um yeah, >> coach, how was this how was this experience for you watching M and how often do you bring players back home? >> No, I I try to do it every year. usually their senior year, so obviously uh this is magnified because again, this is not your normal player. I've been honest with my team. I've been honest with my program, but most importantly, I've been honest with her family. I asked her to have the courage to join me and do something different in a time where she's clearly one of the best players in the country. She won a gold medal for USA basketball. Um the biggest thing I wanted to promise her is there was no fake conversation in the recruiting period, that I was a man of my word, that I ultimately believe in her. Um, I came here to get this program back in the final four, but you need players that can help you do it. And I believe with all my heart and a time and error that a lot of programs take older kids because they want older. I ride with this kid from the first day her freshman year and it's been one fun ride. So to come back home, shout out to Buffalo. Shout out to that women's basketball program cuz a lot of people would not allow to do this. We talked with her coach. She loves Madison. She loves the kids here. She's trying to keep them at home. But for us to bring her back home and let her have her flowers, I can't thank everybody of this community enough. >> Madison, how well do you know some of the UB players? I seen you hugging some in the line after the game. Have you played with them? Just grown up with them and known them? >> Yeah. Um, a little bit of both. Um, some of them I played AU. Some of them um high high school rivals. Um, just all of the above. But it was great seeing them. >> [snorts] >> Uh, do you have any when you were younger, do you have any women or girls that you looked up to from the area that you were uh watching growing up? >> Um, not from the area. No. Um, I really didn't watch much um like UB um growing up um UB basketball. So, >> any other girls or what local girls around your age? Um, I'm trying to like >> think Tony had you in the YMCA so early at 5 in the morning. She didn't get a normal kids life, right? That most kids are staying late at night watching TV. This young lady was in bed cuz Tony and Sophia weren't going to play with you. >> Yeah. Um, no, I mean just like the normal I'll just shout out like you know some of the people I look up to. Diana Sarasi, um, Candace Parker. Um, those are the people that you know I watched growing up. I watched a lot of WNBA um and NBA. So um those were kind of my role models growing up. So >> I want to give a shout out on top of that, you know, to you talk about looking up too. Uh we talked about this when I recruit her. She she told me first thing, "Coach, I want you to know me." I was like, "Okay, Madison, what's up?" And she said, "I want you to know I have a heart for people." And like most kids don't say that. And her family, I can't say enough about Tony and Sophia, her brother Channy was here tonight. And then most importantly, Madison in a time where we travel like no other. God blessed us because the whole TSA shutdown. We We made it here, but we made it here for a purpose. And Madison wanted to go to the Boys and Girls Club. She wanted to give back to those kids, which I thought she did a great job today uh yesterday. And then to think that, you know what, some little girl got the opportunity to hear Madison Francis talk, hear about her dunking in high school, breaking all those records, but most importantly, watching her today. That's what this game was about. And so, I'm happy for her to make an impact, which she's always about. Madison, we talked about you wanting to expand your offensive game. I seen you shooting a few threes you got in the fourth quarter, but how much what can you say about how much you've worked on extending your range as a jump shot? >> Yeah, I mean every day. Um I work with Tony Dukes almost every day. Um just getting my gym in in the gym fine-tuning. Um [snorts] just the little things we worked hard on um postseason um just to get in the gym fine-tuning a little defensive, offensive um you name it. So to see it go in um that's probably what first of the season yesterday. Come on kid. [laughter] See I love her. She's hard on herself. Yeah. >> But here as a coach I want to brag about her too. You know we're talking about you know future pros. What I see in her and we've talked about on film is a future Alyssa Thomas. Lissa Thomas is a a hybrid guard forward who can get rebounds, who can coast to coast. She's I've never had a player in my 20 years that I've been able to coach that said, "You know what? When you get a rebound, be that point guard." All right. And then everybody else can run and our point guards love it. You can see she's able to go coast to coast like she did today. Thought it should be and one, but we're gonna leave out of here. That's for another day. I don't want to get fired. Okay. Uh but just her ability to go the open court. Again, you're watching one of the young ladies who again was ranked top 10 in the country as a freshman by ESPN. Her days of what she's doing, that's why everybody get your popcorn and get your tickets now because you're watching one of the futures right in front of your eyes as a sophomore where I keep telling her just keep being the same kid. In a time and era, people want more. Nuhuh. You know what? You had one hell of a freshman year. Keep enjoying playing the game. Keep enjoying making a difference in people's lives. The stats will take care of itself. But young lady, you're special and that's what you're watching right now. >> Madison, what you think about is it Reese Beanie? >> Uh what you think about her game? How has she been playing this year? >> Oh, her game is like she's ahead of the snake. Like for our team, for her to be that vocal leader for us to control our team when you know things don't go our way. like she's been amazing for us. I mean, every single person on our team um is is impactful and and has a role. So, I'm so proud of my team for supporting me and coming out here and um getting the job done, but this is just the start of what is to come in March. >> Last question. >> How important do you think these non-conference games are? Because the SEC is every year is going to be tough. What What do you want to see in these non-conference games entering before you get into conference play? >> Honestly, just for us to grow. Um the standard is March. the Sanders play in the tournament. So, just the the these little games in non-conference is just chance for grow, chance for mistakes. Um, we're not asking to be perfect. We're not going to be perfect, but just to grow. >> Thanks everybody. >> Thank you. Yeah. Appreciate your support. Expect fishing big time. Yes, sir.
